newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan stainless demand seen up 0.5 pct in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan stainless demand seen up 0.5 pct in 1997/98.

text.p: Domestic demand for stainless steel is expected to rise 0.5 percent to 2,234,000 tonnes in the 1997/98 fiscal year, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Friday.
However, it estimated that exports would fall to 985,000 tonnes from 992,000 tonnes in the current fiscal year, although this could vary depending on exchange rate movements.
The ministry's export estimates were based on current exchange rates.

For the upcoming April-June quarter, MITI forecast Japan's domestic stainless steel demand at 184,000 tonnes per month, off 1.4 percent from 186,700 tonnes per month in the January-March quarter but up 5.1 percent from the same quarter in the prior year.
Stainless steel exports in the April-June quarter were projected at 78,200 tonnes per month, up 10.1 percent quarter-over-quarter but down 12.4 percent year-on-year.
